newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close down, specs liquidate positions.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close down, specs liquidate positions.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower for the second straight session as the industry awaited an official tally on losses from Florida's recent freeze.

"There are still mixed feelings in the market because of uncertainty of what crop estimates are as far as damage," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes, said. "The longs are beginning to give up the ghost."
Some market sources believe losses will have little impact on overall output, since a record crop is expected amid sluggish demand and ample supplies in Brazil.
"There really is not any concern about supply," Ganes said. "We need demand to stimulate the market, and right now we don't have it."
USDA put the Florida crop at 220 million 90-lb boxes.
March FCOJ closed at 83.90 cents a lb, down 0.40, traded 84.10 to 82.60 cents. The back months settled 0.70 lower to 0.75 cent higher.

Celeste Georgakis, an analyst with Dean Whitter, said bearish fundamentals limited this week's rally. The spot March contract ranged to a high of 86.85 cents Wednesday, from Friday's close at 79.90 cents ahead of the freeze.
The bulk of the early and mid oranges have already been harvested, while all of the Valencia's remain on the trees.
Even if as much as 10 percent of the crop was damaged in the freeze, "we would pull back to last year's level which was still an outstanding crop," Ganes said.
